notes: DeepSeek API list prices, USD per 1M tokens, read from api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing on 2026-11-10 (read twice, rows matched). The page has two models: deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) and deepseek-v4-pro (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813).

Each row's own rates are the page's peak rates; offPeak holds its off-peak rates, which are half. peakHours is the page's rule: 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday'. A response is priced by its own timestamp; a sum with no timestamp is priced at peak.
The page excludes Chinese public holidays from the peak hours. They are not modelled, so a response in those hours on a weekday holiday is priced at peak, which is twice what the API would charge.

input is the page's cache-miss price and cacheRead its cache-hit price. The page lists no cache-write price: caching is automatic, and tokens that miss the cache are billed as ordinary input. Cache-write tokens, where an agent reports them, are therefore priced at the input rate in both write columns.
deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are the retired names the page says are 'still accepted' and 'billed at the Flash price'.

deepseek-v4.1-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud are not DeepSeek API ids. They are how OpenCode Go and Ollama Cloud name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in DeepSeek Harness session logs. Neither host has a per-token price list, so that usage is priced at DeepSeek's own Flash rates: what the same tokens would cost at the model maker's API. Remove the two rows to leave it unpriced instead.
deepseek-v4-pro reached through another host (OpenCode Go uses the same id) is priced by its row here, for the same reason.
Search and Fetch ($0.75 per 1,000 successful requests each) are separate APIs. No adapter counts them, so they are not modelled.
Only exact model ids are listed, no prefix keys.
